A user says WorkOS's "extremely pleasant wrapper over SSO and SCIM" made their side project possible rather than "a nightmare of integrations."

A customer says WorkOS saved them tons of time in both engineering and support cases. Their customers often compliment them on how easy SAML and SCIM configuration is, "but it's really WorkOS's wizard that they are complimenting."
One commenter was confused: WorkOS talks about adding all kinds of enterprise features, but their examples and copy mainly show only SSO. They asked whether there is anything else.
A user loves the simplicity and appreciates that WorkOS takes away "the headache that is SSO."

One commenter says it would probably take months to implement SSO with WorkOS's flexibility and ease of use, mainly because of its built-in integrations with so many providers. But "the price is pretty steep," so it would really only suit big-budget enterprise software companies.

A commenter disputes the claim that SSO takes months without WorkOS. They say implementing the OIDC flow from scratch takes half a day to get working and maybe a week to polish, and less with existing libraries.
A commenter comparing WorkOS to Auth0 likes that Auth0 is free for up to 7K active users. By contrast, WorkOS "seems much more expensive out of the gate ($49 per 'connection'?)."

One commenter raised a lock-in concern: you pay a lot for someone else to own critical customer login data. They asked how you would get it out, what that would cost, and whether there are contractual guarantees. They added that migrating away could also require your customers to redo their integration setup.
A user noticed the signup page mentioned Slack for OAuth, but couldn't find that option when setting up an SSO integration. They later said they couldn't find the mention again.

One commenter found the WorkOS careers page broken on Firefox 100/Linux (clicking any opening did nothing). They noted that enterprise buyers judge maintenance and QA quality from public-facing pages.

One commenter argued that an SSO login wall is the most trivial enterprise feature, with plenty of libraries available, so WorkOS "won't be a game changer" with its current feature set. They said compliance, data residency, audit logging, RBAC and similar features would interest customers far more.

A commenter has seen many products hit a brick wall entering enterprise and then stop core work to add hacky versions of required features. They said a developer-friendly SaaS like WorkOS could be a huge win at that inflection point.
An IdP-side admin applauds the WorkOS idea, though they hate the name. They've had dozens of calls walking external dev teams through OIDC, and those teams still couldn't implement it.

Several commenters criticized the naming. They say WorkOS is "not an OS... at best an app framework," and that someone looking for enterprise auth wouldn't search for "work OS." Another said they had no idea what the product was from the landing page.
A commenter in life sciences/pharma said SSO/SAML, SCIM and audit logs were all challenges they had to tackle as one-offs for their SaaS, so they appreciated WorkOS's bundled approach.

A SAML service provider wished WorkOS supplied IdP-specific setup docs (Okta, Azure ADFS) they could hand to their own customers. In their experience, customers only understand their own IdP, and the support burden of SAML is huge.

One user would love to pay for WorkOS but worries that enterprise clients must approve every subprocessor. They wished they could run it under AWS (Marketplace) to avoid requesting signatures from all their clients over personal-data access and jurisdiction.

Asking about the audit trail feature, one commenter said it looks like declaring events as in analytics tools like Amplitude or Mixpanel. They noted the docs didn't explain how the audit trail is made available to end customers.
One commenter said: "I wish I would have found this 3 month ago..." Another noted that RBAC wasn't available yet but called it a very useful product.
